input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting it fixed. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I rely on my mobile internet. Can you help me get the best speed possible?
My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started. What do I need to do next?

Okay, I checked my phone’s status bar. Here’s what I see:
- The signal strength shows just one bar and says “Poor.”
- It says “2G” for the network type.
- There’s a little icon that looks like mobile data is on.
- I don’t see any airplane mode icon.

Is that helpful? What should I do next?

Alright, I changed the network mode to “4G/5G Preferred” like you said. Now my phone shows excellent signal strength and says “5G” at the top. The mobile data icon is still there too.

What should I do next? Will this make my internet speed excellent now?
Oh, I tried to run a speed test just now, but it said “No Connection.” Even though it shows 5G and excellent signal, it seems like the internet still isn’t working. What should I do now?
I checked, and it says my SIM card is active and working. What should I try next?

I looked at my APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet.” There’s also something about an MMSC URL for picture messages, but I’m not sure what that means. I don’t see any error messages. Is this how it’s supposed to look? What should I do next?

I went ahead and reset my APN settings like you suggested. It says the settings will reset when I restart my phone. 

But I’m a bit nervous about rebooting—will I lose any of my photos or anything important if I restart? I really don’t want to lose anything!

I restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says “No Connection.” I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working even though it shows 5G and excellent signal? What else can we try?

Is there anything else we can try before transferring me? I really just want my internet to work at its best speed. I’m not very comfortable with all this technical stuff, and I’d rather not have to explain everything again to someone new if we can avoid it. Is there maybe something simple left to try?

I checked, and Data Saver mode is already off. But it looks like I do have a VPN running—whatever that is. Should I try turning the VPN off? Will that help my internet work better? I’m not sure what a VPN even does.

I turned off the VPN like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says “No Connection.” I’m really starting to worry—why isn’t anything working, even though it shows 5G and excellent signal? Is there anything else we can try? I just want my internet to be excellent.

Alright, if you think that’s the only way, please go ahead and transfer me. I just really hope they can get my internet working at the best speed. Thank you for trying to help and for being patient with me.

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

I can help you troubleshoot and improve your mobile data speed. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID (if you know it)?

Once I have this information, I can check your line and guide you through the steps to improve your mobile data speed.
My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started. What do I need to do next?

First, could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:

Okay, I checked my phone’s status bar. Here’s what I see:
- The signal strength shows just one bar and says “Poor.”
- It says “2G” for the network type.
- There’s a little icon that looks like mobile data is on.
- I don’t see any airplane mode icon.

Is that helpful? What should I do next?

Thank you for the details. Since your phone is connected to a 2G network with poor signal strength, this is likely the main reason for your slow or unreliable mobile data. 2G is much slower than 4G or 5G, and not suitable for most modern internet use.

Let’s try to improve your speed by switching your phone’s network mode to prefer 4G or 5G (if available in your area). Please change your network mode preference to “4G/5G Preferred” in your phone’s settings. If you’re not sure how to do this, I can guide you step by step.

After you change the network mode, check if your phone connects to a better network (like 4G or 5G) and if your signal improves. Let me know what you see after making this change, or if you need instructions on how to do it.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Alright, I changed the network mode to “4G/5G Preferred” like you said. Now my phone shows excellent signal strength and says “5G” at the top. The mobile data icon is still there too.

What should I do next? Will this make my internet speed excellent now?

That’s great progress! Switching to 5G with excellent signal strength should significantly improve your mobile data speed.

To confirm everything is working as expected, please try using your mobile internet for something you usually do (like browsing a website or streaming a video) and let me know if the speed feels much better.

If you want to be sure about your connection quality, you can also run a speed test on your phone. Let me know if you’d like instructions on how to do that, or if you notice any remaining issues with your mobile data.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
Oh, I tried to run a speed test just now, but it said “No Connection.” Even though it shows 5G and excellent signal, it seems like the internet still isn’t working. What should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your phone shows 5G and excellent signal but still says “No Connection” during a speed test, there may be an issue with your mobile data settings or SIM card.

Let’s check your SIM card status next. Please check your SIM card status in your phone’s settings and let me know if it says “Active,” “Missing,” or “Locked.” If you need help finding this, let me know and I can guide you through the steps.
Your SIM card is active and working.
I checked, and it says my SIM card is active and working. What should I try next?

Thank you for checking. Since your SIM card is active and you have excellent signal on 5G, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent your phone from accessing mobile data, even if everything else looks good.

Please check your APN settings and let me know if anything looks incorrect or if you see any error messages. If you’re not sure how to check this, I can guide you through the process. Let me know what you find!

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I looked at my APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet.” There’s also something about an MMSC URL for picture messages, but I’m not sure what that means. I don’t see any error messages. Is this how it’s supposed to look? What should I do next?

Thank you for checking your APN settings. Sometimes, even if the APN name looks correct, there can be issues with the detailed settings (like the MMSC URL) that affect your mobile data and MMS.

To make sure everything is set up correctly, I recommend resetting your APN settings to the default values. After resetting, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your device, or do you know how to do this? Let me know how you’d like to proceed!

APN settings will reset at reboot.

I went ahead and reset my APN settings like you suggested. It says the settings will reset when I restart my phone. 

But I’m a bit nervous about rebooting—will I lose any of my photos or anything important if I restart? I really don’t want to lose anything!

You will not lose any of your photos, messages, or important data by restarting (rebooting) your phone. Restarting simply turns your phone off and back on again, which refreshes its system and applies the new APN settings. All your personal files and apps will remain safe.

Please go ahead and restart your phone now. Once it’s back on, try using your mobile data again and let me know if your internet connection is working properly. If you still have issues, I’ll help you with the next steps.
